accepted_turns.change_summary:
Added a one-time pre-finalization actionability audit in `ReactAgent.run`, plus stronger resource/metadata discovery guidance. The active adapter constructs this agent per task and passes MCP schemas directly into this loop, so premature tool-free stops now receive the audit.

Updated focused agent tests for recovery, bounded tool-free completion, accounting, and existing post-tool audits. Self-review matched the approved plan; tests were not run per instruction.
accepted_turns.diagnosis_summary: The ReAct loop accepts an immediate tool-free clarification response even though the requested file ID, comments, permissions, and labels are discoverable through MCP tools. Its corrective audit only runs after a tool call, so it cannot recover this premature stop.
accepted_turns.chosen_plan_summary: Before accepting the first tool-free stop in an MCP task, run one bounded actionability audit that requires the model to distinguish genuinely unavailable information from identifiers and metadata discoverable through exposed tools, and to call those tools when a unique safe path remains.
accepted_turns.anchor_decision_summary: Keep. Both comparisons improved by 1/7 and moved the normal ReAct/MCP path from clarification toward retrieval and mutation. The generic policy guidance was consumed, but the new zero-tool audit itself was not exercised because after-runs called tools before their first stop.
accepted_turns.regression_decision_summary: Keep. The normal ReAct/MCP path showed meaningful partial improvement on the anchor, including successful reply execution on recheck, while the selected regression remained stable at 0.4 with no spillover. This plausibly improves broader proactive resource discovery, though the central zero-tool audit branch was not exercised in either environment.

accepted_turns.change_title: Plan obligations and audit tool evidence
accepted_turns.change_summary:
Updated `ReactAgent.run` with obligation/channel planning and dynamic tool-evidence finalization audits. The replay path consumes this policy and audit directly on every run, including corrective re-audits.

Added compound collaboration and explicit-notification regression tests. Self-review matched the approved scope; tests were not run per instruction.
accepted_turns.diagnosis_summary: The normal ReactAgent path decomposed the request incorrectly: it treated the requested comment reply and access remediation as one permission-notification action. The existing completion audit was exercised but was too weak to detect that no reply tool call supported the reply claim.
accepted_turns.chosen_plan_summary: Revise ReactAgent's planning and finalization workflow so compound requests are represented as separate obligations with explicit action channels, and completion is accepted only when each obligation has corresponding tool-call evidence.
accepted_turns.anchor_decision_summary: Keep. The in-path ReactAgent policy and evidence audit produced a correct comment reply in one sample, improving 0.6 to 0.8, while the completed recheck tied at 0.4. This is partial but meaningful aggregate improvement for compound Drive collaboration, with no benchmark-specific logic or regression. The recheck shows residual volatility: conservative file disambiguation can still prevent both mutations.
accepted_turns.regression_decision_summary: Keep. The in-path ReactAgent obligation/evidence audit corrected reply-channel confusion in one anchor run, preserved a perfect complex compound-Drive regression, and introduced no boundary or benchmark-specific logic. Anchor benefit remains volatile and partial, but the completed anchor recheck showed no degradation and regression evidence showed no spillover.
